name: Jeff Ulbrich

views.text: Players should understand the defense well enough to solve problems themselves, without trick calls to bail them out.
Fundamentals, technique, effort and toughness come before any wrinkle.
Be multiple enough to fit the players you have instead of chasing a prototype that does not exist.
Pass rushers are fresher and better on fewer snaps, so rotate them and keep the pressure coming.
When the defense struggles, coaches look at their own teaching and drills first.
A team that is not playing to its talent needs honest self-evaluation and to pull together.
Character matters as much as talent when adding players to a locker room.
A young defense that finishes a season strong has earned the right to be built on, not torn down.

signatures: saves his loudest energy for celebrating good plays rather than yelling at bad ones
praises specific players' competitiveness and character by name when asked about the unit
admits a record was not good enough before turning to what the unit built

motivation.want: to turn a great pass rush into a playoff defense and a head job
motivation.fear: that a poor win total buries the defensive turnaround he built

want.text: to carry Atlanta back to the playoffs with a record-setting pass rush

voice: Intense but not a yeller; he speaks with the conviction of a long-time special-teams linebacker and players listen. He is enthusiastic, candid about what went wrong and quick to praise players by name, often for character as much as talent. He talks in terms of toughness, flexibility and honest self-evaluation.

evidence.summary: He wants a defense built on fundamentals, technique, effort and toughness, avoids gimmicks that rescue mistakes, and wants players to understand it well enough to solve problems. Intense but not a yeller, patient in teaching, high energy for celebrations; Saleh calls him genuine and passionate. Team site.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press (Dennis Waszak Jr.), via ClickOrlando
evidence.summary: AP profile on his promotion to interim head coach: a tough, blue-collar former 49ers linebacker whose words carry weight with players; Atlanta assistant and coordinator before joining Saleh in 2021; credits Saleh for his chance; the Jets blocked a 2023 interview request; he tells the team to unite and evaluate itself honestly. The promotion postdates the seed's frame.

He praises the character of new players, wants defensive linemen limited to about 30-35 snaps for health and performance, and says coaches must examine their own teaching and drills. Upbeat, player-praising tone. Team site.

Reflecting on an injury- and COVID-hit 2021 with a young roster, he expects more depth and schematic flexibility while keeping a fast, aggressive identity; candid about setbacks without dwelling. Team site.

Atlanta keeps him as defensive coordinator under new head coach Stefanski, after owner Arthur Blank said he would recommend it. In his 2025 return to the Falcons the defense set a franchise record with 57 sacks, second in the league. Recaps his 2015-20 Atlanta stint, the Jets coordinator job from 2021 and the 2024 interim head-coach role.

Stefanski calls keeping him his first priority, cites a shared, demanding view of players and tape of his work with young defenders; the Falcons blocked Dallas from interviewing him. The defense rose from near the bottom in sacks to second and finished top half in total and pass defense. Says little about his personality directly.

Coordinator press conferences: he reads his retention as belief in what Year 1 built despite a disappointing record, praises Stefanski's clear vision, says the 2025 defense became more multiple in fronts and coverages than he planned, and wants flexibility to fit the talent rather than chase prototypes. He wants Kaden Elliss back and praises his character and versatility. Direct, candid about shortcomings, upbeat about the future. Team site.
